materials.title: The raincoat on the bench
materials.text:
Before our outdoor concert, my new violin case looked suddenly too ____1____ for the approaching rain. Instruments had cover; audience seats did not.

A woman carrying a folded raincoat sat in the front row. I thought she was admirably ____2____. When the first drops fell, however, she spread the coat over an empty place beside her instead of wearing it.

I wondered whom she was ____3____ for. Then a small boy came running from the drinks table, holding two cups carefully. He sat on the covered place and handed one to her. The coat had kept his ____4____ dry.

The rain passed before we began. I concentrated on the music. Wind lifted a page. Our pianist held it down while continuing to ____5____ with one hand. I nearly stopped, but the melody had not disappeared. I kept my part steady until both her hands were ____6____ again.

Afterwards, the woman thanked the pianist for holding the page. I had expected her to mention our loud ending, not the moment I had hoped nobody would ____7____.

She said she used to turn pages for a friend. She knew how much of a performance depended on small ____8____ that the audience might overlook.

Packing up, I saw the raincoat folded under the woman's arm again. The evening had contained several ____9____ plans: a dry seat, a restrained page and a protected instrument. None had been the main ____10____, yet each had allowed it to continue. I had simply become more ____11____ of the work around it. At our next rehearsal, I checked the music stand as well as the ____12____. A secure page would not make me a better violinist by itself, but it could remove an unnecessary ____13____. I placed two clips in my case, beside the spare strings. Preparation could be small enough to ____14____ in a pocket and still make a ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Threatening weather makes the case seem vulnerable/fragile. Weight/emptiness/fame do not explain rain concern.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A carried raincoat suggests preparedness. Loss/boredom/lateness are not the positive weather judgment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: An empty covered seat suggests waiting for a companion. Paying/cooking/voting do not explain reserving that dry place.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The coat covers the place he sits, keeping the seat dry. It does not cover his cup or an instrument.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The pianist continues playing with one hand. Speech/walking/eating are not maintaining the music.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Once the page is secured, both hands are free to play. Cold/empty/hidden do not name released function.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The narrator hopes the near-disruption was unnoticed. Applause/repetition/recording are more specific acts not the basic visibility concern.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Page holding and similar adjustments sustain performance. Prizes/concerts/instruments are not the small actions discussed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Dry seating, page restraint and protection are practical arrangements. Secret/permanent/musical do not cover all three.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: These support the main concert event. Cost/danger/weather are not the concert they allow to continue.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: She becomes aware of supporting work. Shame/fear/tiredness are not the newly appreciative attention.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: At rehearsal she checks stand as well as musical notes. Audience/price are not her playing preparation and weather alone would exclude the musical contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Securing pages removes a distraction. Awards/invitations/melodies are not the unnecessary problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Small clips fit in a pocket. Draw/sing/leak do not express their size compatibility.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Make a difference means have a useful effect. Promise/mistake/noise do not express helpful preparation.

materials.title: The upside-down harbour
materials.text:
Owen tested an old home film before a local history evening. The first image showed boats apparently hanging from the sky. He thought it was a ____1____. The technician adjusted the projector, restoring the harbour’s position.

Watching the test, he realised that simply seeing an image did not mean seeing it under the right ____2____. The equipment and the handling could change what the audience understood.

The technician explained the film’s condition. One short section had been damaged and could not be shown. Owen wanted to fill the ____3____ with a confident description of the missing scene, but nobody present had seen it.

They chose a brief notice instead: a section was unavailable, and the sequence continued afterwards. The notice did not ____4____ the missing content. It showed the limit.

When the audience entered, an older visitor recognised a shop sign in the harbour scene. She had bought bread there as a child. Owen asked if she would write the memory down after the screening, with her name and the part of the film she ____5____. The recollection might help the archive, but it was not something he should silently add as an established ____6____.

The evening included laughter at old fashions and a quiet moment when a now-demolished building appeared. Owen's planned speech became shorter. He let the images run, then invited questions rather than ____7____ every silence.

Afterwards, he thanked the technician. Correcting the inverted picture had been a quick task, but it had changed his ____8____ of presenting historical material. A clear display required more than enthusiasm for the ____9____. It needed attention to the way the evidence reached the room.

He crossed out overconfident parts of his introduction. He listed the source, condition, open questions and ____10____ that prevented claims of completeness. The list did not make the film less ____11____. It gave the audience a firmer place from which to ____12____ it. On the final screen, the harbour lay the right way up. He checked the caption again. The correct ____13____ was only the beginning; the correct ____14____ mattered too. A picture could be clear while its ____15____ remained uncertain.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Upside-down boats initially suggest a joke. Map/receipt/portrait do not explain comic inversion.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Viewing depends on projection conditions. Ownership/price/costume do not describe correct presentation setup.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: He is tempted to fill a missing-sequence gap. Seat/harbour/cup are not absent content.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The notice does not invent what was missing. It explicitly reveals rather than hides; repair would restore footage rather than describe uncertainty.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The visitor identifies the remembered scene. Ownership/projection/destruction are not her viewing act.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: A recollection should not be silently promoted to fact. Plan/joke/invitation do not denote evidential certainty.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: He no longer fills every silence with speech. Measuring/hearing/sharing do not mean talking over it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The incident changes his understanding of presentation. Ownership/collection/address are not the conceptual change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: His enthusiasm concerns historical material, the past. Ticket/weather/fashion are narrower topics that do not describe his interest in presenting the evidence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Limits, such as the missing scene, prevent claiming completeness. Profits/forecasts/decorations do not name those evidential restrictions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Documented limits need not reduce engagement. They do not alter physical damage, missing footage or orientation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Evidence context supports interpretation. Purchase/rotation/repair are not the audience’s reasoning task.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Right way up is orientation. Price/memory/permission do not describe inverted versus upright.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: He also checks the caption/description. Colour/temperature/distance are not the text he verifies.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: A clear image can still have uncertain meaning. Brightness/size/frame concern visible presentation, not interpretation.

materials.title: The story with no single hero
materials.text:
Journalist Erin wrote about an abandoned garden’s reopening. She planned to tell it through one inspiring person’s ____1____.

The first volunteer she interviewed refused the role. He had started the fundraising appeal, but he had not negotiated the lease or planned the paths. A planting volunteer had joined after the early ____2____ were settled.

Erin's notebook grew longer while her opening paragraph remained empty. Each person could explain a part, and each pointed towards someone ____3____. Would the story feel shapeless?

Then she visited on an ordinary maintenance morning. One person repaired a gate while two others sorted tools. A neighbour brought tea and discussed an open-day notice. The project was not a chain of isolated ____4____. Their work overlapped.

Erin asked how a disagreement about opening hours had been resolved. The answer involved several meetings and a trial period. Nobody changed every mind dramatically, but there was a ____5____ people could use again.

She reorganised the article around three decisions rather than three biographies. Within each section, she named the different contributions and checked the account with the people ____6____. No one interview became the authority for everything.

The result still had characters and scenes. It simply resisted assigning all the ____7____ to one hero. Erin kept the first volunteer's lively quotation, but placed it beside the practical work that had made his optimism ____8____.

A reader said the garden sounded like something another group might ____9____. Showing the process had not removed the achievement; it had made some of it ____10____.

Central characters were not always wrong. She had learned to test whether that structure ____11____ the event she was describing. A useful form should emerge from the evidence, not require every contribution to be ____12____ around a preferred figure. The garden had reopened because people performed different tasks and returned when they were ____13____. Her last sentence mentioned the gate. It was small enough to overlook in a grand story, but without it the entrance could not ____14____. The next morning, someone would need to check it ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: A central-person narrative follows experience. Permission/pay/signature alone do not contain the whole reopening story.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Lease/path decisions are early questions settled before planting. Plants/flowers are later material; visitors are not the resolved issues.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Each refers her to someone else with another part. Here/alone/earlier do not complete the other-person referral.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Observed shared work is a set of overlapping actions. Opinions/gardens/interviews are not the maintenance tasks linked.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Meetings and trial form a reusable process. Winner/miracle/secret do not name the accessible method.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: She checks with participants involved in those decisions. Absence/fame/unrelatedness are not the evidential connection.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A hero story assigns credit. Tools/tea/land are physical resources rather than recognition for the result.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Practical work makes optimism possible/grounded. Fashion/cost/privacy do not establish its viability.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: A visible process makes a similar project attemptable. Visiting alone/buying/forgetting do not describe replicating cooperative work.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Showing the process makes the achievement understandable. It does not remove need, hide it or make it identical to all projects.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: She tests fit between narrative structure and event. Replacing/causing/owning the event is not an editorial task.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: A preferred-hero template can force contributions to be arranged around one figure. Forgotten/sold/separated do not describe that central placement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: People return when needed for continuing maintenance. Replacement/applause/completion are not the task-based reason described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: A repaired gate lets the entrance function. Travel/remember/complain are not the entrance’s ordinary operation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Ongoing maintenance requires another check, again. Never contradicts need, yesterday is past and elsewhere changes the gate’s location.
